## DATA NOTES

- Source: ESPN Fantasy API (league, rosters, free agents, transactions, game logs) and ESPN's NBA injury report.
- "Last 15 days" is ESPN's own split; ESPN has no 14-day split.
- Projection line: season averages blended with ESPN's projection (worth 10 games), then 35% weight on the last 15 days.
- Usage %: ESPN doesn't publish it; "usage proxy" is (FGA + 0.44 FTA + TO) per 36 minutes.
- Usable games: days a player gets a starting slot in the best possible lineup (positions respected, best players first); for free agents, days with an open slot he can fill on the current roster.
- Win %: remaining output treated as random around the projection; 70%+ is a likely win, 30% or less a likely loss.
- Role trend: last-5 minutes vs the 10 games before (or season average); 4+ MIN is UP/DOWN. Expected minutes from an injured teammate are an estimate.
- Roster % and its change are across all ESPN leagues.
- Value: average per-game z-score against the rostered players, percentages weighted by attempts and turnovers counted against; about +1 is a first-round player, 0 an average rostered player. Rank is by value in the PLAYER RANKINGS range; L15 Value uses the last 15 days.
- Matchup win chance: categories treated as independent (they're not quite: a big night lifts several at once), so read it as a guide. Category wins are counted, so every expected category matters even when the matchup is decided.
- What it takes: extra output needed over the remaining days to draw even and to reach a 70% chance, with the same per remaining usable game.
- Add/drop simulator: the rest of the matchup re-projected with the pickup in place of the drop; season value is the difference in per-game value.
- Streaming plan: greedy over the acquisitions left; each pickup starts on his first game day and the dropped player keeps his games until the day before.
- Game-to-game value: each recent game scored like the rankings; spread is the standard deviation, floor and ceiling the 20th and 80th percentile, bad games below -0.5.

## DATA NOTES

- Source: ESPN Fantasy API (league, rosters, free agents, transactions, game logs) and ESPN's NBA injury report.
- "Last 15 days" is ESPN's own split; ESPN has no 14-day split.
- Projection line: season averages blended with ESPN's projection (worth 10 games), then 35% weight on the last 15 days.
- Usage %: ESPN doesn't publish it; "usage proxy" is (FGA + 0.44 FTA + TO) per 36 minutes.
- Usable games: days a player gets a starting slot in the best possible lineup (positions respected, best players first); for free agents, days with an open slot he can fill on the current roster.
- Win %: remaining output treated as random around the projection; 70%+ is a likely win, 30% or less a likely loss.
- Role trend: last-5 minutes vs the 10 games before (or season average); 4+ MIN is UP/DOWN. Expected minutes from an injured teammate are an estimate.
- Roster % and its change are across all ESPN leagues.
- Value: average per-game z-score against the rostered players, percentages weighted by attempts and turnovers counted against; about +1 is a first-round player, 0 an average rostered player. Rank is by value in the PLAYER RANKINGS range; L15 Value uses the last 15 days.
- Matchup win chance: categories treated as independent (they're not quite: a big night lifts several at once), so read it as a guide. Category wins are counted, so every expected category matters even when the matchup is decided.
- What it takes: extra output needed over the remaining days to draw even and to reach a 70% chance, with the same per remaining usable game.
- Add/drop simulator: the rest of the matchup re-projected with the pickup in place of the drop; season value is the difference in per-game value.
- Streaming plan: greedy over the acquisitions left; each pickup starts on his first game day and the dropped player keeps his games until the day before.
- Game-to-game value: each recent game scored like the rankings; spread is the standard deviation, floor and ceiling the 20th and 80th percentile, bad games below -0.5.
